name: bounded-line-count
purpose: Count LF bytes in one bounded UTF-8 file and write byte count, LF count, and input SHA-256 as deterministic JSON.
answers_question: Can a standard-library CLI deterministically count LF-delimited lines in this bounded UTF-8 fixture without overwriting an existing report?

inputs.name: --input
inputs.limits: Actual bytes must be no greater than --max-bytes; the evidence run uses 1024.

inputs.name: --max-bytes
inputs.limits: Must be positive; controls the maximum read plus one detection byte.

outputs.name: --output
outputs.format: UTF-8 JSON with sorted keys, two-space indentation, and one terminal LF

exit_codes.3: Input missing, not a regular file, too large, changed beyond the bound, invalid UTF-8, or max-bytes non-positive.
exit_codes.4: Output already exists; it was not overwritten.
exit_codes.5: Output could not be created or written.

side_effects: On success, creates only the explicit output; on output I/O failure a partial newly created output may remain.
determinism: For identical input bytes, Python implementation bytes, and arguments, successful output bytes are identical; paths and timestamps are excluded from output.
provenance: The report embeds the input SHA-256; the evidence receipt pins implementation, input, output, and supporting record hashes.
limitations: The line count is the number of LF bytes. A final non-LF segment is not counted as another line.
The entire bounded input is held in memory.
Only strict UTF-8 regular files are accepted.
The tool does not create missing parent directories.
nonclaims: A successful report does not prove semantic records, newline normalization, or support for other encodings.
The 1024-byte example bound is not a performance claim for larger caller-selected bounds.
